successCriteria.description: The `AuthSession` type exposes the exact canonical shape `{ token: string; profile: EmployeeProfile; status: AuthSessionStatus }`, importing `EmployeeProfile` and `AuthSessionStatus` from `web/src/shared/types/index.ts` (no re-declaration).

`AuthService.login(email, password)` calls `apiClient.login`, persists the returned token via `tokenStorage.setToken`, and resolves an `AuthSession` with `status: AuthSessionStatus.AUTHENTICATED` and the returned `token`/`profile`.
On login failure, the server's error message propagates verbatim with no email-existence hint added, and an already-stored token is left untouched (not cleared).
`AuthService.logout()` clears the token via `tokenStorage.clear()` and is idempotent/safe to call when already logged out.

`AuthProvider`/`useAuth` hold the session in plain React state (no state-management library), expose `login`/`logout`/`session`, and on mount rehydrate an authenticated session from a stored token (re-fetching the profile via `getMe`); anonymous state is `null`.
Vitest unit tests cover login success (token stored + authenticated session returned), login failure (server message surfaced, no email-existence hint), and logout (token cleared).

constraints: The auth module already exists and is fully implemented to spec; no new files or code changes are required this phase — the implementation must remain behaviorally unchanged and satisfy the existing tests.
No state-management library: the session is held in plain React state (useState) within AuthProvider.
The anonymous/not-authenticated state is represented by a `null` session everywhere (service, context, guards) — never an AuthSession object with status ANONYMOUS.
Login failure must not reveal whether the email exists; the server's ApiError.message propagates verbatim with no added hint, and a failed login must not clear an already-stored token.
The auth module depends only on `web/src/shared/types/index.ts` and `web/src/infrastructure/api/index.ts` (via their public entry points); no direct import of module internals.
outOfScope: No new files or code changes are required this phase — the auth module already exists and is fully implemented to spec; the phase is a verification/no-op against the existing implementation.
No state-management library, no UI component library, and no role-gated screens are introduced in this phase.
Client-side JWT expiry decoding is out of scope — token expiry is detected solely via the server's 401 response (handled by the ApiClient, not the auth module).

entityInvariants.invariant: An AuthSession is created only on successful login (or mount rehydration) with status AUTHENTICATED; it is cleared on logout or any 401. There is no anonymous AuthSession object — the not-authenticated state is `null`.

The AuthSession shape is exactly `{ token: string; profile: EmployeeProfile; status: AuthSessionStatus }` — no additional, renamed, or omitted fields; `profile` never carries `passwordHash` or `terminationDate`.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: On failure, the server's error message propagates verbatim with no email-existence hint; a failed login must not clear an already-stored token.
Clears the token and returns to the anonymous (null) state; safe to call when already logged out.
Throws when called outside an AuthProvider; exposes the current session (AuthSession | null) plus login/logout.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: `AuthSession` must import `EmployeeProfile` and `AuthSessionStatus` from the shared types module and reuse them verbatim (no re-declaration or divergence).
`AuthService` must consume `IApiClient` and `ITokenStorage` from the infrastructure API public entry point, and rely on the ApiClient's 401-clearing behavior rather than re-implementing it.

`AuthService.login` must return a session whose `profile` equals the `LoginResponse.profile` returned by `apiClient.login` (the same `EmployeeProfile` shape), and whose `token` equals `LoginResponse.token`.

integrationPoints.why: AuthService delegates login to IApiClient.login and persists the token via ITokenStorage; login failure surfaces ApiError.message.
AuthSession and AuthService assemble the canonical session from these shared types.
useAuth()/AuthProvider supply the session and login/logout that RequireAuth and the login page consume; the null-session contract is what guards test against.
